title: Represent One Whole as a Fraction
goal: I can show that selecting all equal parts names one whole as a fraction.
catchAll: Count every equal part. When the selected count matches the whole count, the fraction equals 1.

teacher.def: The denominator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are in the whole. It is the bottom part of the fraction
A unit fraction is ONE part of a whole. It always has a numerator of one.
The numerator of a fraction tells how many equal parts are being described. It is the top part of the fraction.
A fraction is a number used when a whole is split into equal parts.

glossary.whole: all of one complete shape or the complete distance from 0 to 1
glossary.numerator: the number of equal parts selected
glossary.denominator: the number of equal parts in one whole
glossary.one: the complete whole with no part missing

screens.title: Start with the complete whole
text: One complete disk is one whole.

screens.title: Parts still belong to the same whole
text: Four equal pieces fill the same whole disk.

screens.title: One piece is not the whole
text: One of four equal pieces is 1/4. Three pieces are not selected.

screens.title: Select every piece
text: Now all four equal pieces are selected.
Write 4/4. Nothing is missing, so 4/4 equals 1.

screens.title: A different part size still makes one whole
text: Six equal pieces fill this strip.

screens.title: The endpoint 1 can have a fraction name
text: The unit distance has three equal intervals.
The point at 1 is three intervals from 0, so 3/3 equals 1.

screens.title: Check both counts, not just the bottom
text: A denominator of 8 does not by itself tell whether a fraction equals 1.
This picture has all eight pieces selected: 8/8 equals 1.

sections.heading: Start with the whole
sections.text: Keep the same whole while selecting every equal part. Show that nothing is missing.

sections.heading: Ask your child to show the counts
list: How many equal pieces fill this whole? How many are selected?
What would be missing if only one piece were selected?

sections.heading: Use Help as a teaching step
sections.text: After a mistake, read one short instruction and use its matching picture. Invite your child to point, count and explain before continuing.

sections.heading: Try away from the screen
sections.text: Fold a paper strip into equal pieces. Name the whole, count every piece, then select some or all pieces and explain both counts.

sections.heading: About the assessment
sections.text: These original practice questions are not the teacher’s actual test. The lesson test keeps Help hidden until submission. The written explanation is a self-review with an example or a grown-up, not a computer judgment of mathematical meaning.
